workedTrace: Case: A canary has acceptable latency but new unsupported claims.
Check: Compare canary and baseline for safety, quality, drift, latency, and cost.
Act: Pause expansion and review quality evidence before rollout.
Test: Measure canary quality, safety, drift, latency, and cost against a fixed baseline.

failure.symptom: A canary has acceptable latency but new unsupported claims.
failure.check: Compare canary and baseline for safety, quality, drift, latency, and cost.
failure.fix: Pause expansion and review quality evidence before rollout.

experiment.change: Add one recent failure workflow to the release suite and verify canary response.
experiment.observe: Measure canary quality, safety, drift, latency, and cost against a fixed baseline.
experiment.limit: Canary results apply to its tested traffic and observation period.

masteryQuestion: Hypothetical case: A canary has acceptable latency but new unsupported claims. What evidence decides the first action?
masteryAnswer: Pause expansion and review quality evidence before rollout.

title: Context handling diagnosis
principle: Find what content the model actually received. Count all prompt components and output reserve.
prerequisites: Know the complete request shape and model token limit.
Define the facts and output fields that must survive context reduction.
mechanism: Inspect request size, truncation behavior, stop reason, retrieved chunks, and validation errors. Reduce irrelevant history or evidence.

decision.when: When: The model omits the final instruction after a long conversation.
decision.choice: Inspect token use and prompt assembly, then remove or summarize tested history.
decision.reason: The team raises output tokens when input content was truncated.
decision.reject: Reject this tempting claim: Raising maxTokens can worsen the total budget. Character count is not a reliable token count.

workedTrace: Case: The model omits the final instruction after a long conversation.
Check: Inspect serialized request, token budget, truncation evidence, and stop reason.
Act: Inspect token use and prompt assembly, then remove or summarize tested history.
Test: Measure required content retained in the serialized request and completeness of the answer.

failure.symptom: The model omits the final instruction after a long conversation.
failure.check: Inspect serialized request, token budget, truncation evidence, and stop reason.
failure.fix: Inspect token use and prompt assembly, then remove or summarize tested history.

experiment.change: Change one context component and verify required facts remain in the actual request.
experiment.observe: Measure required content retained in the serialized request and completeness of the answer.
experiment.limit: Token estimation can vary by model tokenizer and request structure.

masteryQuestion: Hypothetical case: The model omits the final instruction after a long conversation. What evidence decides the first action?
masteryAnswer: Inspect token use and prompt assembly, then remove or summarize tested history.

title: Inference integration diagnosis
principle: Classify API errors before changing model or prompt behavior. Preserve the exact request and caller context.
prerequisites: Capture the exact request, operation, model, role, and Region.
Know the API schema and error class for the selected call.
mechanism: Check operation, model identifier, Region, permissions, request schema, size limits, throttling, timeout, and response parsing. Inspect relevant service errors and request IDs.

decision.when: When: A request fails with ValidationException after an API field change.
decision.choice: Compare the serialized request with the operation’s supported schema.
decision.reason: The team retries a malformed request or treats AccessDenied as throttling.
decision.reject: Reject this tempting claim: Do not retry permission failures or invalid requests without a relevant change.

workedTrace: Case: A request fails with ValidationException after an API field change.
Check: Inspect operation, serialized fields, model identifier, role, Region, and error code.
Act: Compare the serialized request with the operation’s supported schema.
Test: Measure whether the corrected request succeeds under the same role, model, and Region.

failure.symptom: A request fails with ValidationException after an API field change.
failure.check: Inspect operation, serialized fields, model identifier, role, Region, and error code.
failure.fix: Compare the serialized request with the operation’s supported schema.

experiment.change: Change one request field and replay the same call under the same role and Region.
experiment.observe: Measure whether the corrected request succeeds under the same role, model, and Region.
experiment.limit: Service errors can change. Use current service documentation and logs.

masteryQuestion: Hypothetical case: A request fails with ValidationException after an API field change. What evidence decides the first action?
masteryAnswer: Compare the serialized request with the operation’s supported schema.

title: Prompt behavior diagnosis
principle: Treat prompt quality as a testable interaction among instructions, evidence, examples, and output contract.
prerequisites: Keep fixed cases and a versioned prompt baseline.
Know the required response contract and evaluation rubric.
mechanism: Use a fixed failure set and compare prompt versions. Check instruction conflicts, missing context, examples, variable substitution, and schema validation.

decision.when: When: A prompt update improves tone but causes required fields to disappear.
decision.choice: Compare schema validity and task criteria across the old and new prompt versions.
decision.reason: The team rewrites several instructions at once and cannot identify the cause.
decision.reject: Reject this tempting claim: Adding more instructions can create conflicts and consume the evidence budget.

workedTrace: Case: A prompt update improves tone but causes required fields to disappear.
Check: Diff prompt versions and rendered variables, then inspect failures against the rubric.
Act: Compare schema validity and task criteria across the old and new prompt versions.
Test: Measure rubric failures and schema validity after changing one prompt component.

failure.symptom: A prompt update improves tone but causes required fields to disappear.
failure.check: Diff prompt versions and rendered variables, then inspect failures against the rubric.
failure.fix: Compare schema validity and task criteria across the old and new prompt versions.

experiment.change: Change one instruction or example and measure exact failure categories on fixed cases.
experiment.observe: Measure rubric failures and schema validity after changing one prompt component.
experiment.limit: Prompt improvements may not transfer to unseen tasks.

masteryQuestion: Hypothetical case: A prompt update improves tone but causes required fields to disappear. What evidence decides the first action?
masteryAnswer: Compare schema validity and task criteria across the old and new prompt versions.

title: Retrieval defect diagnosis
principle: Trace a missing or poor answer backward from generation to indexed source data.
prerequisites: Know source versions, sync state, chunking, and embedding settings.
Prepare labeled queries and expected retrieval results.
mechanism: Check source existence, latest sync, extraction quality, chunk boundaries, metadata filters, embedding compatibility, and ranking. Compare query and document vector configuration.

decision.when: When: A current policy exists in storage but never appears in retrieved evidence.
decision.choice: Check ingestion state and filters, then inspect the indexed version and top results.
decision.reason: Changing the model prompt hides a stale index or wrong embedding setup.
decision.reject: Reject this tempting claim: A model upgrade cannot reliably fix missing or unauthorized evidence.

workedTrace: Case: A current policy exists in storage but never appears in retrieved evidence.
Check: Inspect source sync, chunk boundaries, embedding settings, filters, and ranked evidence.
Act: Check ingestion state and filters, then inspect the indexed version and top results.
Test: Measure source freshness, relevant retrieval, and latency after the ingestion or query fix.

failure.symptom: A current policy exists in storage but never appears in retrieved evidence.
failure.check: Inspect source sync, chunk boundaries, embedding settings, filters, and ranked evidence.
failure.fix: Check ingestion state and filters, then inspect the indexed version and top results.

experiment.change: Update one source record and trace it through ingestion and retrieval with a labeled query.
experiment.observe: Measure source freshness, relevant retrieval, and latency after the ingestion or query fix.
experiment.limit: A successful sync event does not prove useful retrieval.

masteryQuestion: Hypothetical case: A current policy exists in storage but never appears in retrieved evidence. What evidence decides the first action?
masteryAnswer: Check ingestion state and filters, then inspect the indexed version and top results.

title: Prompt maintenance diagnosis
principle: Manage prompt templates as versioned application dependencies. Test variables, schema, and release links.
prerequisites: Know the prompt resource version and required variables.
Keep a known-good request trace and schema validation result.
mechanism: Inspect unresolved variables, incompatible request fields, prompt version, and changed instructions. Compare logs and traces with a known-good version.

decision.when: When: A deployed prompt version returns literal placeholder text.
decision.choice: Inspect variable names and values at invocation, then test the rendered prompt.
decision.reason: The stored template looks correct while runtime parameters are missing or stale.
decision.reject: Reject this tempting claim: A stored template does not prove that runtime variables have valid values.

workedTrace: Case: A deployed prompt version returns literal placeholder text.
Check: Inspect prompt version, variable bindings, request fields, schema result, and trace.
Act: Inspect variable names and values at invocation, then test the rendered prompt.
Test: Measure rendered variable correctness and output validity for each prompt version.

failure.symptom: A deployed prompt version returns literal placeholder text.
failure.check: Inspect prompt version, variable bindings, request fields, schema result, and trace.
failure.fix: Inspect variable names and values at invocation, then test the rendered prompt.

experiment.change: Change one template variable contract and compare rendered requests and output validity.
experiment.observe: Measure rendered variable correctness and output validity for each prompt version.
experiment.limit: Logs can contain sensitive prompts and need strict access and retention.

masteryQuestion: Hypothetical case: A deployed prompt version returns literal placeholder text. What evidence decides the first action?
masteryAnswer: Inspect variable names and values at invocation, then test the rendered prompt.
